question.text: Prakash Ventures is computing WACC for investee Nalanda Edtech. Cost of debt (pre-tax) = 11%; tax rate = 25%; Cost of equity (CAPM, unlisted-adjusted, inclusive of any illiquidity premium) = 16%. Capital structure: Debt:Equity = 2:3. What is the WACC?

explanation.text: The Logic: Post-tax Kd = 11% x (1 - 0.25) = 8.25%. Weights: D = 2/5 = 40%, E = 3/5 = 60%. WACC = 0.40 x 8.25% + 0.60 x 16% = 3.30% + 9.60% = 12.90%. Per Section 14.6 Box 14.1 (p. 376), post-tax cost of debt must be used. The keyed answer is therefore 12.90%. The Trap: Option B (13.00%) uses pre-tax Kd. Option C (13.50%) uses D:E = 50:50 weights. Option D (14.30%) uses pre-tax Kd combined with the wrong 50:50 weighting; it is included as an additional incorrect distractor. Note: The original item contained a fourth option that ALSO began with "12.90%" (with an unsupported "post deduction of illiquidity" qualifier), creating avoidable numeric ambiguity since two options had the correct WACC value. That duplicate has been replaced with a materially different incorrect value (14.30%) so option A is now the uniquely correct answer. Source: FINAL_Series-XIX-C_AIF Managers_Ver-Dec-2025.pdf, p. 376.
